producer_report.summary: I fixed the one place where a retry lost accepted corrections: a retry of a retry. A failed job's own corrections were already carried, so I couldn't reproduce a loss for a plain failed job. When the job being retried was itself a retry, only its own corrections reached the reader brief. The corrections given to the jobs earlier in the chain were dropped. I replaced `original_request` in reading.rs with `earlier_jobs`, which returns the chain of earlier jobs. `earlier_attempt` now prepends their corrections, oldest first and redacted, ahead of the retried job's own. The original request is still carried as before. I added three tests in reading.rs: a failed job's corrections in order and redacted, a failed job with no verification record, and a failed retry that inherits its predecessor's corrections. I added one briefs.rs test that a failed earlier attempt lists its corrections under the existing corrections heading, in order. I added a Fixed entry to CHANGELOG.md. All three checks pass.
open_issues: I could not reproduce the exact 9e8t/hrdp loss from the code alone. The retry-chain loss is my best match for the report. Without that history I can't confirm it is the case the user hit.
crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs and crates/athena-core/src/store.rs are listed as deliverables but I did not change them; no change there was needed.
I did not change how a chain's corrections are deduplicated. A user who repeats a correction on the retry sees it twice.
mistakes: I did not write the new tests first, so I never saw them fail. The chain test would fail on the old code, because it drops the first job's corrections. The other new tests pass on the old code too, because they cover paths that were already correct.
learnings: A failed job's own corrections were already carried by earlier_attempt/carry. Only the retry chain lost them: original_request followed the chain for the request text but not for corrections.
reader_brief already prints an earlier attempt's corrections whatever its failed flag, so briefs.rs needed only a test.
desires: A way to read the persisted tool output file; a hook blocked it, so I re-ran the tests quietly.
